input_contract: canonical 500 ppi 8-bit grayscale PNG, one frame, non-interlaced

steps.action: decode the PNG container directly: signature, per-chunk CRC, IHDR, IEND
steps.rationale: a decoder handed a paletted or gamma-tagged file returns a grayscale raster anyway, having applied a colour policy this project never chose

steps.action: require exactly one channel (PNG colour type 0)
steps.rationale: a three-channel source would be silently averaged by most loaders

steps.action: require exactly 8 bits per sample; 1, 2, 4 and 16 are refused
steps.rationale: libpng converts 16-bit down without saying so, which changes the pixels

steps.action: no inversion: ridges stay dark on a light background
steps.rationale: upstream trained on this polarity and nothing in the artifact declares another
every upstream crop rule is corpus-specific (SFinGe, MCYT)

steps.action: none: this variant has no localization branch
steps.rationale: the checkpoint contains no localization weights

steps.action: no pose estimation, rotation correction or realignment
steps.rationale: alignment would be a component the artifact does not supply

steps.action: pad symmetrically to a square of side max(width, height)
steps.rationale: the model asserts a square 299x299 input; the aspect ratio is preserved rather than stretched

steps.action: fill with 255 in the 8-bit domain, which is exactly 1.0 after the conversion
steps.rationale: white is the background of a canonical fingerprint image; upstream pads with 1.0

steps.action: left = top = floor(total / 2); right = bottom = total - left
steps.rationale: upstream applies the same floor to both sides and then asserts squareness, which cannot hold for an odd difference
DEEPPRINT_INPUT_SIZE is asserted by the pinned stem
the library default is a library decision and can move between releases
downsampling without it aliases ridge frequencies, and the default has changed before
the pinned stem takes one channel

steps.action: [0, 1] by exact uint8 / 255, applied before padding and resizing; the antialiased resize may leave a sample up to 2**-20 outside that range and is not clamped
steps.rationale: converting first keeps the resize in float instead of quantizing through 8-bit intermediates, and matches upstream's own order; the resize computes its filter weights in float32 and they do not sum to exactly one, so a uniformly white image lands a few ulps either side of 1.0, and clamping it back would change pixels in a step neither the spec nor upstream performs

steps.action: none: no mean, no standard deviation, no contrast or histogram transform, no ridge enhancement
steps.rationale: any of them would be an undeclared component of the algorithm
the stem takes one channel, not three

steps.action: none: the canonical PNG bytes are decoded once and never re-encoded
steps.rationale: a round trip through an encoder could change a sample and would not be visible
